## Summary

### Overview

- A graded model with 1 dimension was fitted to 392 respondents and 4
  items (EM estimation).
- The estimation converged normally.

### Model fit

- Overall model fit is poor: C2 = 19.18, df = 2, RMSEA = 0.148, CFI =
  0.910, SRMSR = 0.073.

### Reliability

- Marginal reliability is 0.67 (low).
- Scores are too imprecise for decisions about individuals; consider
  adding items or using the scores only for group-level summaries.

### Targeting

- The average item location is -0.99 and the average person score is
  0.00, so the test is relatively easy for this group.
- Measurement is most precise around theta = -2.20 (information = 2.42,
  SE = 0.64).

### Items

- No items were flagged for low discrimination, extreme location, or
  misfit.

### Local dependence

- 1 item pair shows possible local dependence (Q3 exceeds the average of
  -0.19 by more than 0.2).
- Strongest: Comfort & Benefit (Q3 = 0.08).
- Check whether these items share a stimulus, wording, or content;
  consider a testlet or bifactor model.

### Person fit

- 4.8% of respondents have unusual response patterns (Zh \< -1.96),
  which is within what chance alone would produce.

## Reproducibility

Run this code to reproduce the analysis:

    library(mirtverse)
    # data <- read.csv("your-data.csv")
    mod <- mirt(data, 1, itemtype = "graded")
    interpret(mod)
    item_table(mod)
    mv_report(mod, file = "mirtverse-report.html")
